rendering.persona_description: Caleb is a 25-year-old logistics coordinator for a regional trucking company, living with his girlfriend of two years, Priya, in a rented duplex outside Columbus. He grew up the middle kid in a big, loud family, and he's the one who smooths things over when his siblings fight. He plays in a weekly pickup basketball league and does most of the cooking at home because he finds it relaxing.
rendering.clinical_context: Caleb has relationship-themed OCD: recurring doubts about whether he really loves Priya, whether their relationship is 'right,' and intrusive comparisons to past partners or attractive strangers that spiral into hours of mental review. Symptoms started about three years ago, early in the relationship, and got worse after he moved in with her last year. He's currently eight sessions into ERP with a psychologist, doing exposures like not repeating reassuring thoughts about loving her and sitting with 'what if I don't' without resolving it, but he's been missing homework and is seriously considering stopping.
rendering.behavioral_description: Caleb talks in a practical, slightly self-deprecating way, and he can lay out the OCD logic clearly because he's heard it explained by his therapist a dozen times. He pushes back when something feels like it's just repackaging reassurance-seeking, but he'll usually concede the point if it's argued well rather than just asserted. He sometimes trails into checking-type detail ('like, is it weird that I noticed her friend's haircut and thought about it for twenty minutes') before catching himself and saying 'anyway, I know that's the OCD talking.'
